Centre for Financial and Monetary SystemsCentre for Financial and Monetary SystemsConnecting leaders to create a financial system that allocates capital to support planet, people, and communities.We work towards a more sustainable, resilient, trusted, and accessible financial system.Our vision is to connect leaders to design and develop a financial system that effectively allocates capital and investment in support of planet, people, and communities.The Centre for Financial and Monetary Systems provides an independent and impartial platform to connect leaders seeking to build a more sustainable, resilient, trusted, and accessible financial system that reinforces long-term value creation and economic growth.250+Centre Partners12+Initiatives5CommunitiesOur initiatives on financial and monetary systemsOur initiatives focus on making the global financial system more inclusive, efficient and aligned with long-term economic and societal goals.Financing the Real Economy TransformationMobilizing capital across infrastructure, heavy industry and transport, food systems and nature to support a more resilient, competitive and investable global economy.Longevity EconomyIncreasing public-private collaboration and designing frameworks that build financial resilience.Global Retail InvestingFostering action to improve retail investor participation in capital markets and promotes responsible investing.AI in Financial Services Developing guidance for public and private sector entities as they navigate the various stages of AI adoption.Our impactWe work with public and private partners to strengthen financial systems and improve how capital is allocated to support people, the planet and economic stability.Highlight opportunities for access as capital markets transformThe global financial system is undergoing several simultaneous transformations. Capital markets continue to be transformed through digitalization and democratization. Both investors and corporate issuers have changing needs and expectations, and a range of new actors are joining traditional financial institutions to meet this demand. Establishing guardrails to protect the integrity of the global financial systemEvolving geopolitical conflicts have caused disruptions throughout the financial system and could create further turbulence as states engage in geoeconomic statecraft and increasingly use the financial system to advance their geopolitical ambitions. Our reports Financial and Monetary Systems...Regulation of Digital Assets in a Shifting Global LandscapeDigital assets are moving beyond a stand-alone market and becoming part of the financial infrastructure. As this transition accelerates, regulation will shape not only market integrity and financial stability but also monetary sovereignty, capital flows, sanctions enforcement and the future competitiveness of financial systems. Developed by the World Economic Forum and Boston Consulting Group, Regulation of Digital Assets in a Shifting Global Landscape examines how jurisdictions can build credible regulatory frameworks for digital asset markets. Drawing on regulatory developments across 35 jurisdictions and extensive engagement with public- and private-sector leaders, it identifies nine dimensions that policy-makers must consider, from legal certainty and custody to digital money, financial crime, market integrity and infrastructure. The report offers a practical playbook to help jurisdictions at any point in their current digital assets regulatory journey assess risks, sequence priorities and determine where existing rules are sufficient or require adaptation. It also explores how regulatory cooperation, common standards and cross-border trust can support safe institutional adoption while preserving legitimate national choices.28 October 2026Stakeholder Capitalism...The People Premium: Human Capital as a Driver of Value Creation in Private MarketsHuman capital is increasingly recognized as a critical driver of value creation in private markets, yet the industry lacks a common approach to embedding, measuring and attributing its impact across the investment life cycle. AI is also both a new source of competitive advantage and a disruptive force. As competition for returns intensifies, investors are increasingly viewing human capital and operational excellence as interconnected levers of long-term value creation. This report draws on the experience and perspectives of leaders in the field to identify emerging business practices across the investment life cycle. It examines five themes and translates them into practical insights for investors and portfolio company leaders seeking to strengthen human capital as a strategic value-creation lever.30 September 2026Financial and Monetary Systems...The AI Playbook for Financial ServicesRecent advancements in generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping financial services at an intense pace. As institutions move from experimentation to scaled deployment, the central challenge is integrating AI with both urgency and discipline.24 June 2026Financial and Monetary Systems...The Longevity Dividend: The Business Case for Linking Health and WealthThree low-tech interventions could save the world’s healthcare systems more than $5.8 trillion and unlock another $645 billion in productivity by 2040. Fall-proofing homes, increasing levels of physical activity and expanding the use of hearing aids are affordable and simple examples that produce considerable returns when they are understood in the wider context of the longevity economy. This report demonstrates how co-ordinated approaches that link health improvements to financial resilience will yield multitrillion-dollar opportunities in the years to come.23 June 2026Financial and Monetary Systems...Deepening Divides: The Cost of a More Fragmented Financial System2025 and early 2026 marked a turning point for the global trade and financial systems as states deployed economic statecraft on a scale not seen in the modern era, accelerating and deepening fragmentation. These global trends present concrete risks and opportunities to emerging markets and developing economies, which are explored in detail in a case study of major African economies. The report offers new quantitative analysis and renews the private sector’s call to preserve the core elements of the global financial system that enable economic growth and long-term prosperity. 04 June 2026Financial and Monetary Systems...The Future of Venture Capital: Unlocking Liquidity and GrowthVenture capital has evolved from a niche financing mechanism into a central pillar of the global innovation economy, managing $3.5 trillion in assets and backing more than 250,000 companies over the past two decades. Today, however, the model faces a period of significant transition, marked by slowing capital recycling, an uneven global distribution of scale-ups and the rapid reshaping of venture economics by artificial intelligence. Drawing on original data analysis and perspectives from leading general and limited partners, the report offers a comprehensive assessment of the structural shifts under way, setting out five strategic priorities to strengthen the industry and sustain its critical role in financing global innovation.11 May 2026Join us in shaping the future of financial and monetary systemsWe believe that progress happens by bringing people together. People from all walks of life, who have the drive and the influence to make a positive change.
